rationale: C21 is a direct drafting precursor: it announces the forthcoming executive order and lays out its distinctive organizational design, names, reporting relationships, division of functions, and effective date. The child implements those instructions in operative legal form. C23 is also highly relevant as the existing foreign-aid administrative order whose functions and machinery the child transfers and preserves, while C06 supplies an older version of closely related machinery. C21 is strongest because its provisions map specifically and sequentially onto the child's central reorganization.

shared_material.child_excerpt: all functions ... of the Foreign Operations Administration ... are hereby transferred to the Secretary of State and the Department of State
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I shall issue ... an Executive Order transferring the affairs of the Foreign Operations Administration, except for certain military functions which are charged to the Defense Department, to the Department of State as of June 30, 1955.
shared_material.explanation: The letter expressly previews the central transfer later enacted by the child, including the military-functions exception and timing.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of State shall establish ... an agency in the Department of State which shall be known as the International Cooperation Administration.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A new semi-autonomous organizational unit, to be known as the International Cooperation Administration, will be established in the Department of State, to carry out the transferred functions.
shared_material.explanation: The distinctive agency name, departmental placement, and purpose are carried directly into the operative order.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The International Cooperation Administration shall be headed by the Director of the International Cooperation Administration ... The said Director shall report directly to the Secretary of State.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Provision will be made for a Director of the International Cooperation Administration ... The Director ... will report directly to the Secretary of State
shared_material.explanation: The child closely follows the letter's named leadership and direct-reporting structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The said Administration ... and all functions transferred by this Part shall be subject to the direction and control of the Secretary of State.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The policy authority then fixed in the Secretary of State is now extended to include supervising authority over operations. The Executive Order will provide for this.
shared_material.explanation: The child converts the announced supervisory arrangement into operative direction-and-control language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of State, after consultation with the Secretary of Defense, shall make appropriate arrangements for carrying out the function of coordination
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Secretary of State will be responsible for coordinating all Mutual Security programs, which will of course include the establishment of arrangements with the Secretary of Defense
shared_material.explanation: Both prescribe the same State–Defense coordination machinery.
